name: Visit monitoring
plain: iOS reports the places a person stays at (arrival and departure) without constant GPS.
meaning: Infers home, work and frequent stops with low power. The app gets coarse arrival and departure times and places, a daily routine map.

android.api_surface: Activity Recognition Transition API (ACTIVITY_RECOGNITION) and geofence dwell transitions
android.note: No place level visit API for third parties; dwell via geofence loitering delay

ios.persistence: Delivered after the fact, relaunches app
ios.note: Visits delivered with arrival and departure dates and a coordinate with horizontal accuracy; delay minutes to hours

limits.headline: Can learn which places you stay at, with arrival and leave times, on iPhone
limits.user_action: You allow Always location for a feature that keeps a place history or journal
can: Learn about stops, like home, work or a cafe, without constant tracking
Get arrival and departure times plus a rough spot on the map
Wake up in the background when a visit is noticed
cannot: Report a visit right away; delays can run from minutes to hours
Work at all without Always location
Know what you did there, only where and when
Match this on Android, which has no visit service for apps; it must guess with geofences
limits.reach_label: Ongoing, but only places you stay
limits.differs: iPhone has a built in visit service. Android has none for outside apps and has to guess from geofences.

story.what_it_is: iPhone can tell an app when you arrived at and left a place you stay, without constant GPS.

marketing.name: Visit monitoring
marketing.pitch: Apple offers a low power way to be told when a person arrives at or leaves a place where they spend time.

story.for_you: You never see it. An app quietly learns that you spend nights at one place and days at another, which can power helpful suggestions or a very detailed routine map.
story.for_makers: Makers can learn home, work and frequent stops cheaply. It powers place memory and context features, and it is sensitive because routine shows who you are.

use_cases.example: A map app builds a timeline of places you visited today.
A journaling app adds the cafe where you wrote an entry.
An ad company infers which stores you visit most for audience groups.
A fitness app notices you are at the gym and offers to start a workout.
A loyalty app counts a visit to the store without any check in.
A research app measures how long people spend at parks.

story.android_note: No exact match for third party apps. Apps use geofences with a dwell delay.
story.ios_note: Visits come with arrival and departure times and a spot, but delivery can lag by minutes to hours.
